Compare all three methods

The earlier Jev-alone calls used different prompt wording and ran at different times. Those differences prevent this comparison from isolating the effect of the proposal. Choose a completed condition with usable confidence scores.

Least-confident firstRandom selection expectationJev alone

The source runs on every row. Curves reuse cached outcomes; they do not measure dollar or latency savings. Random accuracy and balanced accuracy are exact expectations; random macro-F1 uses 10,000 draws with Monte Carlo error, not a confidence interval. Sequence scores include the class ID and end-of-sequence token and are not calibrated confidence.

This selection rule needs further testing. This analysis uses one split, with 114 Breast Cancer cases and 36 Wine cases, and followed inspection of earlier results. Test labels were not used to rank rows or choose the review fractions. The fraction that performs best here still needs validation on new data. Sources that always chose one class, missing probabilities and incomplete reviews are excluded.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY IN THE PROMPT?

A class proposal, without source identity

Jev sees the original row, the same training examples and the proposed class. It receives no model name, rationale or confidence.

These historical pairwise comparisons overlap and were made at different times. They are not independent repeatability trials. Matching returned model IDs do not prove the serving backend was unchanged.

INTERPRETATION

Does the proposed class help?

A pipeline can improve on its source LLM and still perform no better than Jev alone. The controls below keep the rest of the prompt fixed to test whether the proposed class helps.

An allowed category can still be the wrong answer. These public test datasets may have appeared in model training. The results cover one split and calls made at different times.

MATCHED PROPOSAL CONTROLS

Actual proposal · none · shuffled

Does the actual proposal help?

A positive difference (A minus B) means the actual proposal performed better on the selected metric. Corrected / harmed counts show how answers changed from B to A.

Failures count as incorrect. A pending arm has no published score, even when some of its requests have returned. No threshold or overall winner is selected here.

SEPARATE SERVING DIAGNOSTIC

Do identical prompts agree?

These repeats were selected before execution. Agreement uses only pairs with two valid responses; reference-only, repeat-only and joint failures remain separate. Agreement does not establish accuracy or deterministic serving.

CONTROL RESULTS AFTER RETRIES

What changes after failed calls are retried?

Uses the dataset and metric filters above. First-attempt controls remain the primary result.

Separate recovery evidence and limitations ↗

RETRY RESULTS

Compare first attempts and retry results

A retry is an additional attempt and cost. Successful recoveries do not erase historical failures. A previously skipped review gets its first service call after the source proposal is recovered. Recovered metrics are a separate descriptive view of the same cases; they do not create a new independent test set.

Failures count as incorrect · incomplete conditions remain unscoredEvidence & limitations ↗
